column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 class mappings

#mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 LinkML schema. CALM Control maps to the CSF Subcategory (the leaf-level actionable outcome); ControlRequirement maps to CSFCategory (the grouping level); the Architecture document relates to CSFDocument; responsible parties in CALM flows relate to CSF ResponsibleParty.

column7: A CALM Control is an atomic, domain-scoped security requirement attached to architecture elements; a NIST CSF 2.0 Subcategory is the leaf-level outcome statement (e.g. ID.AM-01) - both represent the implementable leaf unit of a control framework.

A CALM ControlRequirement defines the specification for a control domain; a CSF Category groups related subcategory outcomes under a CSF Function - both model the intermediate grouping layer of a control taxonomy.

A CALM Architecture is the technical system under governance; a CSF Document is the policy/profile artifact expressing the security posture - the Architecture is the subject that a CSF profile governs.

A CALM Flow describes business processes mapped to architecture relationships; a CSF Function (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) describes a high-level cybersecurity activity - both organise related security activities at the process level.

A CALM Decorator attaches supplementary references and data to architecture elements; a CSF Link connects a CSF element to an external informative reference - both add contextual cross-references to primary model elements.
